text: The following question stood in the name of  Ms Joan Pereira –  16 To ask the Minister for Health whether polyclinics can scale up their capacity to accommodate more walk-in patients with urgent medical conditions, such as those experiencing acute or severe pain, and to avoid turning away senior citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
text: At the same time, we will work with GP clinics, which play an important role in treating acute diseases at the primary care level, too.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: We do have situations where residents have not only not been served as a walk-in – they could not get a place for walk-in – but even for online booking, where the night before they could not get a slot.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I just want to ask the Senior Minister of State whether the Ministry of Health (MOH) is looking at improving this situation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: But it seems that is not helping much.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Is there a need to change the scheme or the policy so that it becomes attractive for patients to use the GP clinics as well, and not all going to the polyclinics?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: On both his questions, he has highlighted the direction in which we are moving, which is for the polyclinics to work in partnership with the GP clinics and family practitioners in the area that they serve.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do want our residents to understand that these are part of a continuum of primary care services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For the polyclinics, if the patient turns up without an appointment, wants to walk in and if they have an urgent need, they will be attended to.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There will be triage, they will be assessed and, if there is an urgent need, they will be attended to.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If it is something elective and there are no appointment slots left, the recommendation will be that they seek care electively in a planned way, make an appointment with the GP within the vicinity.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I am not sure whether there are specific details about how the Member feels the CHAS scheme is not helping much.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Perhaps if there are specific cases, we could look into that and see how we can assist.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In general, we are trying to find ways to help the GPs, the family physicians, as a community, upskill and deliver these types of cares in partnership with the polyclinic teams as well.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In general, the GPs and the family physicians are more than willing and able to do so.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: For the residents in the west, especially in the Nanyang ward, they go to Pioneer Polyclinic.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: They really have difficulties getting appointments online and, even so, when the residents go to the polyclinic early in the morning to queue for the appointment, they cannot get an appointment.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, my supplementary question is, one: when they queue, if they cannot get an appointment, can they get the next day's appointment?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Two, we also understand that most of the polyclinics and the MOH building are in other parts of Singapore, in the north-west part or the western part, and not in the Jurong area.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, how are we going to alleviate the situation at Pioneer Polyclinic?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We will look at his suggestion in terms of the queuing system and the appointment booking process.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are trying very hard to improve the service provision for primary care by both expanding our network of polyclinics, as well as leveraging on the experience and capability of the GP clinics and family physicians that are in the community and that can serve this resident population very well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I am asking this supplementary question on behalf of Ms Joan Pereira who is on medical leave.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: She has a very strong conviction about asking this supplementary question, so I am conveying this question to the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Can the Senior Minister of State consider asking polyclinics to consider prioritising walk-in patients who are seniors?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Because Ms Joan Pereira is very particularly interested in making sure our seniors walking in, as well as those with mobility issues, are attended to, given that they may find it challenging to go to the GPs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think the Senior Minister of State has highlighted it somewhere at the beginning, but I think it is very, very focused on seniors – whether there could be prioritising for them, especially those who are very aged and have mobility issues.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think the right thing to do is to allow the professional judgement of the clinical team at the site to make the assessment as to the urgency of their needs, rather than set a very arbitrary cut-off in terms of an age, for example, or other factors where actually the key thing is to assess the needs of that patient at that time.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And that is, indeed, what the clinical services will do.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: A number of my Clementi residents are quite concerned about the implications of the online booking process for polyclinic appointments.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State whether MOH is looking at the take-up of these online bookings, whether there is a trend towards fewer seniors being able to get these online bookings and whether the seniors are as able to attend the polyclinics as before?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And so, the senior residents within the geographical area are, indeed, attending, are able to access the services and receive the care from the polyclinic care teams.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But as I said, I would be happy to look at the data, specifically, if he would like to file a related question.
